assessment: The incumbent supplies removable partitions already assembled and checks an order slip, providing an opportunity to verify the requested configuration. Repeated three-compartment orders approach the time target (D2-O6), so assembly is not uniformly slow. Mixed batches contain every extreme delay, but layout complexity and switching are confounded. Missing/incorrect-part reports and unpacking confusion show checks and the generic diagram do not reliably secure the outcome (D2-O3/O4). Concrete limitation: insertion-retry widths overlap first-pass widths (D2-O5), weakening a simple width-only account without excluding slot fit, orientation or handling. These are synthetic observations, not established causal explanations.

openings.claim: Preparing an order-specific parts set and checking it against the selected layout before insertion may reduce mixed-batch selection mistakes and delays.
openings.delta: Replace repeated shared-bin selection during assembly with a bounded per-order selection and verification step; retain full assembly and reversible joints.
openings.prediction: Within the same layout and worker, prepared sets reduce selection/checking time or detected component discrepancies; insertion time may remain unchanged. Unchanged selection performance would weaken this account.
openings.probe: Use spare-board samples in counterbalanced matched runs, recording selection, insertion, checking and packing separately. Include set preparation in total time and inspect final parts/count/color. Gate adoption on measured cost limits and available time before the fixed delivery date.
assumptions: Layout-specific required parts can be derived from existing templates and order slips.
Preparation does not consume more time or bench capacity than it saves; cost and schedule feasibility remain unmeasured.

openings.claim: A diagram of the customer's ordered layout explicitly locating the short partition may improve unaided arrangement.
openings.delta: Replace the three-layout diagram with order-specific placement guidance, without changing components or rearrangeability.
openings.prediction: Customers receiving the specific diagram make fewer short-partition placement errors and achieve their ordered layout more often; persistent failures suggest guidance alone is insufficient.
openings.probe: Assign the ten willing participants across existing versus specific diagrams, balancing layout and prior exposure. Verify complete kits beforehand; record unaided success and placement errors. Treat this small comparison as directional evidence; verify production outcomes in the 60-unit pilot.
assumptions: Diagram preparation and printing fit both cost caps and the fixed deadline.
Previously observed participants may have learned the layouts, limiting generalization.
